claims.text: The sources move the name from Jacob to household, tribes, kingdoms, and a later argument that distinguishes Israel within Israel.
Deuteronomy denies size as the basis of election, Amos makes special knowledge a reason for punishment, and Romans keeps privilege beside mercy and judgment.
The sources preserve a mixed departing company, foreign prayer, an outsider’s appeal, grafted branches, and a multinational multitude without using one mechanism of belonging.
Prophetic and apostolic sources appeal to remembered covenant, remnant, gathering, reunited houses, new covenant, and mercy.
Romans distinguishes ancestry, promise, remnant, hardened branches, Gentile inclusion, fullness, and mercy across one sustained argument.
Revelation numbers sealed tribes, sees an uncountable multinational multitude, and inscribes tribal names on the New Jerusalem’s gates.
